Investigators said he admitted to throwing her across a room, causing her to strike a shelving unit and land on the bed, where a bucket of hardware and tools came crashing down and knocked her to the floor. He told detectives that the next day, the baby had "pulled a hot iron down from a shelf in the bedroom," which landed on her thigh and caused a large burn. According to police, Dunn said several times that he was "too busy" to get Ja'Leah medical care until she stopped breathing later Saturday evening, which is when he called 911. When first responders arrived at his house, they found Ja'Leah unresponsive with a large burn to her left thigh and "bruises all about the body" and a diaper that appeared several days old, police said.

cases.name: Stasy J. Charles
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She attended kindergarten in Haiti before coming to the United States in September 2008 at the age of six with her brother Christopher Charles and her parents Jeannette Charles and Jerry Charles. She began school in New Orleans from first grade through high school, graduating from John Ehret High School in 2020. She then attended Louisiana State University (LSU) in Baton Rouge.

Stasy was a sweet, loving, and talented young woman. She loved people deeply, sang and danced at church events, and participated in cheerleading. Her Catholic faith was an important part of her life. She loved Haitian food, enjoyed doing hair and makeup, and always sought ways to help others, often asking her mother to send money to support their family in Haiti. Stasy had a playful sense of humor, especially at her mother’s friends’ homes, where she always made her presence known with laughter and a love for food. She was the first child on her mother’s side and grew up caring for her younger siblings, often serving as her parents’ little helper and babysitter. She had a beautiful gift for making people feel seen, always offering compliments and encouragement."
cases.narrative:
Police located her, lying in the parking lot suffering from several large stab wounds.

Preliminary reports are Heinrich arrived at Charles’s residence and began ramming her vehicle with his vehicle. He exited his vehicle and forcibly removed Charles from her vehicle, at which time he began to stab her repeatedly. Heinrich fled the area and intentionally entered the oncoming lane of travel, resulting in a head-on collision with another vehicle. While seated in his vehicle after the crash, he lit himself on fire.

Officers responding to the scene were able to extinguish the flames and he was transported to a local hospital with life
threatening injuries. He died the following day.
